# Gwydir Forest Park - Ty’n Llwyn, near Betws-y-coed

![](https://cdnfd.cyfoethnaturiol.cymru/693182/natural-resources-wales_10852_not-required-_no-identifiable-individuals_no-restrictions.jpg?rmode=min&width=1024&height=500&quality=80&v=1da0014384f06a0)

## Welcome

The Ty'n Llwyn car park is the starting point for a walking trail to the famous Swallow Falls waterfall.

The Swallow Falls Trail goes through woodland to a viewpoint over the waterfall - you get a great view from this side of the river so don’t forget your camera.

Ty’n Llwyn means “house in the grove” in Welsh and it is a great place to enjoy a picnic with a view at one of the tables around the car park.

![""](https://cdnfd.cyfoethnaturiol.cymru/ud5emj1e/tyn-llwyn-picnic-area.jpg?width=500&height=333.33333333333337)

## Walking trail

The walking trail is waymarked from start to finish.

Look out for the information panel at the start of the trail.

[Find out about walking trail grades.](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/things-to-do/walking-trail-grades-and-other-information/ "Walking trail grades and other information")

### Swallow Falls Walk

- Grade: Strenuous
- Distance: 2.2 miles/3.6 kilometres
- Time: 1½-2½ hours
- Trail information: This circular trail is mainly on steep rough narrow paths less than 70 cm wide in some places, on unmade and uneven surfaces, where you can expect mud, rocks and tree roots. There are several ﬂights of steps on the trail and a bench at the waterfall where you can rest and admire the view. There is a wheelchair accessible picnic table in the car park.

From the car park, the path descends through the woodland and the sound of the river gets louder as you approach Swallow Falls and the viewpoint.

![""](https://cdnfd.cyfoethnaturiol.cymru/svcmc21r/tyn-llwyn-swallow-falls-viewpoint.jpg?width=500&height=333.33333333333337)

The path then winds its way up through trees and rocky outcrops to another viewpoint with views of Moel Siabod.

![""](https://cdnfd.cyfoethnaturiol.cymru/in1nsdmc/tyn-llwyn-moel-siabod-viewpoint.jpg?width=500&height=333.33333333333337)

## Accessibility information

Facilities for visitors with disabilities at Ty'n Llwyn include:

- car parking spaces for Blue Badge holders
- dusted paths lead from the Blue Badge car parking spaces to wheelchair accessible picnic tables with beautiful views

## Gwydir Forest Park

Ty'n Llwyn is in Gwydir Forest Park.

Gwydir Forest Park lies in the heart of the Eryri National Park and encircles the village of Betws-y-coed.

Lead and zinc mining once dominated the area and the legacy of old engine-houses, waste tips and reservoirs are characteristic features of the forest landscape today.

Several of the most important mines have been partially restored and made safe for visitors.

Waymarked trails start from Betws-y-coed and several other Natural Resources Wales car parks in Gwydir Forest Park:

- [Betws-y-coed](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-betws-y-coed/ "Gwydir - Betws-y-coed") \- peaceful forest walks away from the tourist bustle
- [Cae'n y Coed](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-caen-y-coed/ "Gwydir - Cae'n y Coed") \- easy-to-find picnic area and walk with panoramic mountain views
- [Cyffty Mine](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-cyffty-mine/ "Gwydir - Cyffty Mine") \- short trail around abandoned lead mine
- [Dolwyddelan](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-dolwyddelan/ "Gwydir - Dolwyddelan") \- walking trail along Roman road and cycle trail with mountain views
- [Hafna](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-hafna/ "Gwydir - Hafna") \- walking trail through lead mine ruins and red-graded mountain bike trail
- [Llyn Crafnant](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-llyn-crafnant/ "Gwydir - Llyn Crafnant") \- walking trails around the lake and accessible riverside trail
- [Llyn Geirionydd](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-llyn-geirionydd/ "Gwydir - Llyn Geirionydd") \- picnic site with walking trail around two beautiful lakes
- [Llyn Sarnau](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-llyn-sarnau/ "Gwydir - Llyn Sarnau") \- picnic spot with a walk to two scenic lakes
- [Penmachno](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-penmachno/ "Gwydir - Penmachno") \- remote mountain bike trails with spectacular views
- [Sawbench](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-sawbench/ "Gwydir - Sawbench") \- two red-graded mountain bike trails and historical walk

## Eryri National Park

Gwydir Forest Park is set in Eryri National Park.

Eryri is the largest National Park in Wales and is home to picturesque towns and villages and the highest mountain in Wales.

It is looked after by the Eryri National Park Authority.

For more information about visiting Eryri go to the [Eryri National Park Authority website](https://www.snowdonia.gov.wales/visiting).

## Visiting safely

We want you to return home safely after your visit here.

You are responsible for your own safety as well as the safety of any children and animals with you during your visit.

For advice and tips to help you plan your visit here go to [Visiting our places safely](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/visiting-our-places-safely/ "Visiting safely").

## Changes to visitor facilities

See the top of this webpage for details of any planned closures or other changes to visitor facilities here.

For your safety, always follow instructions from staff and signs including those for trail diversions or closures.

We may divert or close trails whilst we undertake maintenance work or other operations and we may need to close other visitor facilities temporarily.

In extreme weather, we may close facilities at short notice due to the risk of injury to visitors and staff.

## **Organising an event on our land**

You may need permission from us to organise an event or to carry out some activities on our land.

[Check if you are allowed to use our land.](https://naturalresources.wales/permits-and-permissions/using-land-we-manage/check-if-you-are-allowed-to-use-land-we-manage/ "Check if you are allowed to use land we manage")

## How to get here

We recommend you follow these directions or use the Google map below which has a pin on this place’s location.

Ty’n Llwyn is 3½ miles west of Betws-y-coed.

Take the A5 from Betws-y-coed towards Capel Curig.

Go past past the Cae'n y Coed car park and turn right onto the narrow minor road immediately before the Ugly House (Tŷ Hyll).

The small car park is 1 mile up this road, on the right.

The postcode is LL24 0DH. **Please note that this postcode covers a wide area and will not take you directly to the entrance.**

[View this place on the What3Words website.](https://what3words.com/added.opts.shave "View this place on the What3Words website")

### Public transport

The nearest mainline railway station is in Betws-y-coed.

For details of public transport go to the [Traveline Cymru website](https://www.traveline.cymru/ "Traveline Cymru website").

## Parking

Parking is free of charge.

Overnight parking is not permitted.

## Contact details

There are no staff at this location.

[Contact our customer team for general enquiries](https://naturalresources.wales/about-us/contact-us/general-enquiries/ "General enquiries") during office hours, Monday to Friday.

generation_excerpts: The Ty'n Llwyn car park is the starting point for a walking trail to the famous Swallow Falls waterfall.
The Swallow Falls Trail goes through woodland to a viewpoint over the waterfall - you get a great view from this side of the river so don’t forget your camera.

- Grade: Strenuous
- Distance: 2.2 miles/3.6 kilometres
- Time: 1½-2½ hours
- Trail information: This circular trail is mainly on steep rough narrow paths less than 70 cm wide in some places, on unmade and uneven surfaces, where you can expect mud, rocks and tree roots. There are several ﬂights of steps on the trail and a bench at the waterfall where you can rest and admire the view. There is a wheelchair accessible picnic table in the car park.
From the car park, the path descends through the woodland and the sound of the river gets louder as you approach Swallow Falls and the viewpoint.
